about: Plausibility rules for decoded shared-model values, read by tools/model-checks.py. `keys` holds one rule per model key, written as a pack writes it (`lat`, `track.confidence`); a rule applies to the key at the top of an entity and in every list item. `min` and `max` are inclusive and a value that is not finite fails them; `one_of` lists the values allowed; `one_of_meaning` takes the allowed values from the key's meaning in model/*.def (the comma-separated words after the last colon). `meaning_rules` apply to every key of a type whose meaning begins with a prefix. `order` states that one key of an entity is not earlier than another. `synthetic` names the packs that exercise rules of the specification with edge values on purpose. `datum` is the vertical-datum check of pack.md. Add a rule here, with its reason; no code changes.

lat.reason: latitude in degrees, WGS 84: the poles bound it

lon.reason: longitude in degrees, WGS 84: -180 and 180 are the same meridian, both admitted

hae.reason: the deepest ocean floor is about 11 km below the geoid, which lies within 110 m of the ellipsoid; the top admits geostationary orbit (3.6e7 m), lunar distance (3.8e8 m) and the Sun-Earth L1 and L2 points (1.5e9 m), the farthest places a ground system still reports as a geodetic height

ce.reason: an error radius is not negative; one larger than half the Earth's circumference (2.0e7 m) says nothing a smaller one does not. CoT's 9999999 for 'unknown' is inside

le.reason: an error bound is not negative; the top is the top of hae

course.reason: degrees true; 360 is admitted as the same direction as 0

speed_ms.reason: a ground speed is not negative; 100 km/s is above the fastest meteor entering the atmosphere (72 km/s) and every spacecraft relative to the Earth

time_ms.reason: epoch milliseconds UTC from 1980-01-01 to 2100-01-01: GNSS time begins 1980-01-06 and a two-digit year 80 reads as 1980, so no report a pack carries is older; a format's own epoch (NTP 1900, Unix 1970) is that format's zero, not a report time. Below the window is a relative time (since boot, of the day, of the week) or a counter decoded as an epoch time, or a format's epoch not added; above it, a sentinel or a unit error

time_error_ms.reason: a bound, not an offset: 0 or more (model/core.def)

track.sigma_east_m.reason: a standard deviation is not negative; top as ce

track.sigma_north_m.reason: a standard deviation is not negative; top as ce

track.sigma_up_m.reason: a standard deviation is not negative; top as le

track.vel_east_ms.reason: a component of a velocity is not faster than the speed bound of speed_ms

track.class.reason: the classes model/track.def lists in the key's meaning

detection.range_error_m.reason: a standard deviation is not negative

detection.cross_range_error_m.reason: a standard deviation is not negative

detection.radial_velocity_error_ms.reason: a standard deviation is not negative

meaning_rules.reason: a flag is 1 when the source states it and 0 when it denies it (spec/shared-model.md, Types and units)

order.reason: a report does not go stale before the time it is valid

synthetic.reason: these synthetic formats exist to exercise the rules of the specification with edge values on purpose (the largest integer, a value a transform refuses, a non-finite derivation); a vector is skipped when its pack, its source or its target is one of them

datum.about: A pack that maps a height key names the vertical datum of that height in its pack.md. A height key has a unit of height_units (m or ft; FL is barometric by its unit, and raw keys of no unit are not read), and its name has a token hae, height, altitude, alt, elevation, ele, elev, amsl, msl, agl or hgt, or its meaning has the word height, altitude or elevation; unless its name or meaning is about an error, a resolution, a size or a depth (not_height). A key whose meaning says it is above the WGS 84 ellipsoid (and is not the geoid, and not 'not above') is an ellipsoid key: a passage of its pack.md about a height must name the ellipsoid, since a height above mean sea level mapped to it unconverted is wrong by up to 110 m.

not_height_keys.n2k.ship_sheight: a vessel's dimension, not the height of a position

datum.reason: seven engines that agree on a height do not show which height it is; core hae is above the WGS 84 ellipsoid, and a pack that does not say what its source measures from cannot be checked
datum.terms_about: Each term is a regular expression matched against each passage of pack.md (a paragraph, a table row, a list item) that has a height word or the name of a mapped height key, case-sensitive except inside (?i:...). The vocabulary: the ellipsoid, mean sea level (the geoid), barometric (pressure altitude, a flight level), above the ground or a local origin (take-off, home), and an explicit statement that the source names no datum, which is a statement too.
